articles.title: Faith-Labor Organizing: Why Building Permanent Infrastructure is the Intervention This Moment Demands
articles.content_excerpt: Featured image by Jared Rodriguez. Our congregations and our unions each have a measure of power. None of it is enough. The change we seek requires building power together; prioritizing building that power together in parallel with the work we are already doing alone. Our faith communities and labor unions share geographies, serve many of the same families, and claim a common commitment to human dignity. We rarely build power together. When we collaborate, the collaboration tends to be transactional: labor shows up for a rally the church organized, a pastor blesses a picket line. The event ends. Everyone goes home. articles.title: Trump’s Greenland Deal Puts His Annexation Plans on Ice
articles.author: Huw Paige
articles.content_excerpt: Donald Trump recently concluded an agreement with the governments of Greenland and Denmark over the status of the Arctic island. Trump presented it as a big victory for his efforts, claiming that it granted the United States “permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland, completely addressing ALL of our many US concerns.” The substance of the agreement told a different story. After doing lasting damage to the relationship between the United States and Europe, the Trump administration got more or less the same deal it could have obtained by asking politely. Trump’s repeatedly stated plan to acquire Greenland has been put on the back burner. articles.author: Buffalo DSA
articles.content_excerpt: On Thursday, members of our Steering Committee and endorsed candidate Adam Bojak met privately with Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. We were proud to share how we are building a durable, sustainable socialist project here, as well as share our hope to see Rep. AOC coordinate more strongly with the growing socialist bloc forming at every level of elected office. Afterward, a range of our chapter organizers joined Team AOC for their Project Reactivation event. Regardless of what her political career holds, one thing is clear: Rep. AOC and her team would not have visited Buffalo, or prioritized a private sit-down with Buffalo DSA leaders, without the diligent work of our members. articles.title: We Have to Figure Out How to Design a Warming Planet
articles.author: Marianela D’Aprile
articles.content_excerpt: Before we get into the nitty-gritty, we should start with the problem in its purest form: The world as we know it cannot go on. Something’s got to give. Ideally, that would be capitalism, but we don’t have enough time to pull that off before the planet catches fire. The planet is already catching fire. What to do, then? Everything — supply chains, information systems, labor practices, policy decisions, economic structures­ — is so inextricably linked that it feels impossible to know where to start chipping away. articles.title: Mark Carney Is Taking Aim at Canada’s Labor Movement
articles.author: Adam D. K. King
articles.content_excerpt: On September 21, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government introduced legislation that could amount to one of the most significant rollbacks of workers’ rights in Canada since the creation of the postwar industrial relations system. Tucked inside the sprawling 232-page Bill C-39 are amendments to the Canada Labour Code that would give the federal labor minister explicit authority to terminate lawful strikes and impose binding dispute resolution when the minister decides a work stoppage threatens the “national interest.” The legislation would also create a new “special mediator,” adding an additional state-directed phase to collective bargaining. articles.title: The Dilemmas of Socialist Governance of a Capitalist State
articles.author: Max Elbaum
articles.content_excerpt: Since the 2016 combination of Donald Trump’s election and Bernie Sanders’s breakthrough campaign, efforts to synergize grassroots organizing with electoral engagement have become a priority for both long-standing and new radical formations. The dominant strategy is for socialists and progressives to run as Democrats aiming to both block MAGA’s drive toward US-style fascism and to win a measure of Left “ governing power .” In the last year, such efforts have yielded impressive results. Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist, is mayor of the nation’s largest city. Abdul El-Sayed, an outspoken advocate for Medicare for All and Palestinian rights, won the Democratic nomination for US senator in Michigan. articles.title: A Labour Prime Minister Inaugurated Britain’s Neoliberal Era
articles.author: Neil Warner
articles.content_excerpt: When Britain’s Labour Party met for its annual conference in September 1976, the government headed by its leader, James Callaghan, was confronting a severe economic crisis. This included the combination of high inflation and unemployment (“stagflation”) and a currency crisis that would, by the end of the year, lead the government to arrange a loan from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). IMF assistance came with the requirement of steep budget cuts. In this context, conference delegates passed ambitious resolutions that condemned cuts and called for nationalization of much of the financial sector as well as extensive controls over the movement of capital, imports, and company investment decisions.
